svg.text: Worked example: one image, fifteen pins, six layers
Every figure below is the actual output of a single pipeline run. No value is illustrative.
1402 x 1121 PNG · 1.89 MB · analysed in 19.4 s
Wholly synthesised by a generative model, not a manipulation of authentic content
Decided on documentary provenance. Detector agreement raised confidence but did not determine the verdict.
DOCUMENTARY AND PHYSICAL EVIDENCE · RAN CONCURRENTLY
7 C2PA byte markers found in container
2 focus regions on the combined map
ELA and attention did not converge
Consistent with synthesis, not local editing
Two independently derived methods, one finding.
6,915 TOKENS · 26.1 s · TRANSCRIPT RETAINED FOR AUDIT
The verdict rests on Tier 1 documentary evidence. The C2PA manifest read by PIN-A2 declares the image wholly synthetic, produced by OpenAI
through GPT-4o and ChatGPT. That is the producer's own signed assertion, and it outranks any inference drawn from appearance.
Confidence is reduced from the 0.93-0.98 band to 0.88 because the cryptographic signature could not be validated: the certificate has
expired. The unvalidated manifest still carries the declaration, which is why the verdict stands while the confidence does not.
PIN-B4 classified the image as Deepfake. The manifest declares trainedAlgorithmicMedia, meaning wholly generated rather than composite,
so the correct taxonomy is AI_GENERATED. A classifier's inference about category does not override a declaration of origin.
PIN-D1 reports near-zero spatial agreement between the detectors, which weakens the reading of their consensus without disturbing the
Tier 1 finding. PIN-A3's six anomalies are supporting evidence only: on a PNG source the premise of Error Level Analysis is weakened.
